🐾 Why do dogs pull on leash?

Most dogs pull because it works.

❌ Leash gets tight
➡️ You keep walking

That pattern repeats… so your dog learns pulling works.

You can try this:

⛔ Stop every time the leash gets tight
✔️ Wait for your dog to come back beside you

And yes, that can help.

But it often turns your walk into this:

🚶‍♀️ stop… start… stop… start…

And your dog still may not understand what to do instead.

There is another way to look at it.

✔️ When we change what gets rewarded
✔️ We change the choices our dogs make

And that is where things start to feel different 🐶❤️

When your dog is anxious, everything feels harder:
Walks. Visitors. Even bedtime.

And here’s the truth most people miss:
Training only works when your dog’s brain is calm enough to learn.

That’s where the right kind of support comes in.

Before anything else, look at what stress actually looks like in your home:
• Barking at every little noise
• Pacing or panting at night
• Clinging to you constantly
• Shaking during storms or fireworks
• Restlessness even after walks

These aren’t “bad habits.”
They’re signs your dog’s nervous system is overloaded.
